title: A field that is present but unset is never initialised, and the response echoes whatever was in that memory
index_line: T-0040 · AUTH_DECISION · presence check stands in for assignment; the unset struct member is reflected, leaking session tokens (an uninitialised-memory INFO_LEAK whose use is session hijack — also search INFO_LEAK) · c/perl/python/java · corroborated
invariant_violated: Parsing is assumed to fully populate the structure it returns: if a field is present in the request, its destination has a value. But 'present' and 'has a value' are different facts, and a parser that checks only presence leaves the destination untouched. From then on the field holds whatever the allocator last left there — and any code that copies it out, logs it, or puts it in a response is now publishing memory.

mechanism.does: the attacker posts the login form with the username parameter present but carrying no value
the parser sees the field and records that it is present, so it never enters the branch that would assign it
the structure that maps the request is emitted with that member left exactly as allocated — uninitialised, not empty
the backend builds its authentication XML from that structure and copies the member into the response as-is, up to the first zero byte
the response carries a run of process memory, which on a busy VPN concentrator includes other sessions' tokens
repeating the request harvests enough tokens to hijack an authenticated session — an information leak that becomes an authentication bypass

source.http.body.value: a form field that is *present without a value* — the payload is an absence, which is why input filters and big-payload probes never see it

sink.file.read.value: the copy-out of the structure member into the response/XML builder — the over-read happens at the serializer, not in the parser

lifetime.object.value: the uninitialised struct member: allocated once, never written for this request, read anyway

oracle.channel.value: the response body itself — the leaked bytes come back, so extraction needs no timing or error oracle

preconditions.expr: a request-to-structure binding that checks presence separately from assigning the value
the unset member reaches an output path (XML response, log line, error message) without being re-checked
the process handles concurrent sessions in the same address space, so the leaked bytes are other users' secrets

check.spec: send the empty field repeatedly on a lab instance with a second live session and check whether the responses differ in content

success: a response field contains bytes the request never supplied, and the content changes between requests
the value disappears when the field is omitted entirely and returns when it is present-but-empty — that asymmetry is the bug
harvested bytes include tokens or session identifiers usable as another user
failure_like: the binder assigns an empty value on presence, or the structure is zeroed before parsing
false_positive: reflection of the empty field as an empty string — the safe behaviour
a response containing cached data from the same session — reproduce with two sessions before claiming cross-user leakage

hazards: the bug lives in the gap between the parser's contract and its implementation, so reading either alone will pass it — compare what the struct looks like for (omitted) vs (present-empty)
the leak is amplified by concurrency: the value is whatever the previous occupant of that heap left, so exploitation is statistical, not deterministic
the sanitizer that keeps being proposed for this class (zero-fill the struct) is a language-level fix; the copy-out is the sink to audit
response-type validation ('the XML looks well-formed') is not validation — the garbage can be well-formed
non_transfers: memory-safe languages where an unset member is nil/null and the serializer refuses or emits nothing
parsers that treat missing and empty identically and always write the destination

evidence.target: Citrix NetScaler ADC / NetScaler Gateway as Gateway or AAA virtual server (CVE-2025-5777, CitrixBleed 2)
